verses.text: The gospel kicks off, Jesus Christ the Son of God, no intro needed.
As it’s written in Isaiah’s scroll: “Yo, I’m sendin My hype man before You, He gon clear the lane.”
Voice in the wild sayin: “Prep the road for the Lord, smooth it out, no potholes.”
John popped up in the desert, droppin baptism vibes, preachin squad repentance for forgiveness.
Whole Judea and Jerusalem fam pulled up, confessin sins, gettin dunked in Jordan.
John’s fit? Camel drip, leather belt, locusts and honey diet—man was raw.
He said: “One stronger than me comin, I ain’t worthy to untie His kicks.”
I dunk y’all in water, but He gon dunk y’all in Holy Spirit fire.
Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, got baptized by John in Jordan.
Straight up, when He came out the water, heavens opened, Spirit slid down like a dove.
Voice from heaven: “You My Son, My fave, I’m vibin heavy with You.”
Spirit instantly yeeted Him into the wilderness.
He was out there forty days, tempted by Satan, chillin with wild beasts, angels servin Him.
After John got locked up, Jesus came to Galilee, droppin gospel of the kingdom.
He said: “Time’s up, kingdom of God is here. Repent, believe the gospel.”
Walkin by Galilee sea, He saw Simon and Andrew throwin nets—they were fishers.
Jesus said: “Follow Me, I’ll make y’all fishers of people.”
They instantly dropped nets, followed Him.
He saw James and John in the boat with Zebedee, fixin nets.
He called them, they bounced on pops Zebedee with hired crew, followed Him.
They hit Capernaum, straight to synagogue on Sabbath, Jesus started teachin.
People were shook—He taught with authority, not like the scribes.
In synagogue, a dude with unclean spirit popped off.
He yelled: “What You want, Jesus of Nazareth? You here to destroy us? I know You—the Holy One of God.”
Jesus clapped back: “Shut it, come out.”
Spirit threw the man down, screamed loud, dipped.
Everyone was shook: “New teaching with authority—He even bosses spirits, they obey.”
His fame went viral all over Galilee.
Straight out the synagogue, He went with James and John to Simon and Andrew’s crib.
Simon’s mother-in-law was sick with fever, they told Jesus.
He pulled her up, fever bounced, she started servin them.
That evening, after sunset, people brought all the sick and demon-possessed.
Whole city crowded the door.
He healed many sick with various diseases, cast out many demons, didn’t let them speak—they knew Him.
Early morning, before sunrise, He dipped to a quiet spot, prayed.
Simon and crew hunted Him down.
They said: “Everyone lookin for You.”
He said: “Let’s bounce to nearby towns, I gotta preach there too—that’s why I came.”
He went through Galilee, preachin in synagogues, castin demons.
A leper came beggin: “If You will, You can make me clean.”
Jesus felt compassion, touched him: “I will, be clean.”
Instantly leprosy dipped, he was clean.
Jesus charged him, sent him away quick.
He said: “Don’t tell anyone, but go show yourself to priest, offer what Moses commanded, proof for them.”
Dude went out, blasted it everywhere, so Jesus couldn’t openly enter cities. He stayed outside in desert spots, yet people came from everywhere.
Few days later He pulled back to Capernaum, word spread quick He was home.
Squad packed the crib, no space left, not even at the door, He was droppin the Word.
Four dudes pulled up carryin a paralyzed bro.
Couldn’t get in cuz of the crowd, so they went roof mode, broke it open, lowered the mat right in front of Jesus.
Jesus saw their faith, said to the paralyzed bro: “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
Some scribes sittin there, thinkin in their heads,
“Why He talkin like that? That’s blasphemy vibes. Only God forgives sins.”
Jesus instantly clocked their thoughts, said: “Why y’all thinkin sus stuff in your hearts?”
“What’s easier: say ‘your sins forgiven’ or ‘get up, walk’?”
“But so y’all know Son of Man got authority to forgive sins…” He said to the paralyzed bro,
“I say to you, get up, grab your mat, bounce home.”
Dude instantly stood, picked up mat, walked out in front of everyone. Crowd was shook, glorified God: “We never seen anything like this.”
Jesus went out by the sea, crowd pulled up, He taught them.
He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sittin at tax booth, said: “Follow Me.” Levi got up, followed Him.
Jesus chilled at Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners sat with Him and His crew—lots of them followed.
Scribes and Pharisees saw Him eatin with sinners and tax collectors, said to His disciples: “Why He eatin with them?”
Jesus heard, said: “Healthy don’t need a doc, sick do. I came not for righteous, but for sinners.”
John’s disciples and Pharisees were fasting. They asked: “Why do John’s disciples and Pharisees fast, but Yours don’t?”
Jesus said: “Can wedding guests fast while groom’s with them? Nah.
But days comin when groom’s taken away, then they’ll fast.”
“No one patches old drip with new cloth, it tears worse.
No one pours new wine in old skins, it bursts. New wine goes in fresh skins.”
One Sabbath He walked through grainfields, His crew started pluckin heads of grain.
Pharisees said: “Look, why they doin what’s not lawful on Sabbath?”
Jesus said: “Did y’all not read what David did when he was hungry, he and his crew?
How he went into God’s house in Abiathar’s priest days, ate the showbread, which only priests can eat, and gave to his crew too?”
He said: “Sabbath was made for humans, not humans for Sabbath.
So Son of Man is Lord even of Sabbath.”
He pulled up again to the synagogue, and a dude was there with a dead hand vibe.
They were watchin Him sus, tryna catch Him healing on Sabbath so they could cancel Him.
He said to the man with the dead hand: “Step up front.”
He asked: “Is it lawful on Sabbath to do good or do evil, save life or kill?” They stayed ghost silent.
He looked around heated, grieved at their hard vibes, said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched, and it was restored.
Pharisees bounced out, linked with Herod’s crew, plotting how to end Him.
Jesus dipped with His disciples to the sea, crowd from Galilee followed, plus Judea,
Jerusalem, Idumaea, beyond Jordan, and Tyre and Sidon fam—big crowd heard His moves, pulled up.
He told His disciples to keep a boat ready cuz crowd was pressing.
He healed many, so whoever had sickness was tryna touch Him.
Unclean spirits saw Him, fell down, shouted: “You the Son of God.”
He charged them not to make Him known.
He went up a mountain, called who He wanted, they came.
He appointed twelve, called them squad, to be with Him, send them to preach,
and to flex authority to cast demons.
Simon He named Peter,
James son of Zebedee and John his bro—He named them Boanerges, sons of thunder,
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Canaanite,
and Judas Iscariot, who later betrayed Him. They rolled with Him.
They went home, crowd gathered again, couldn’t even eat.
His fam heard, said: “He’s outta His mind,” tried to grab Him.
Scribes from Jerusalem said: “He got Beelzebub, casts demons by prince of demons.”
He called them, dropped parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?”
“If a kingdom beefs with itself, it collapses.
If a house beefs with itself, it falls.
If Satan beefs with himself, he’s done.”
“No one can rob a strong man’s crib unless he first ties him up, then he can loot.”
“Truly, all sins and blasphemies will be forgiven to humans.
But whoever blasphemes against Holy Spirit never gets forgiveness, guilty forever.”
They said He had an unclean spirit.
His mother and bros came, stood outside, sent for Him.
Crowd sat around Him, said: “Your mother and bros outside seek You.”
He answered: “Who is My mother, or My bros?”
He looked around at those sitting: “Here are My mother and bros.
Whoever does God’s will is My bro, sis, and mother.”
He started teachin by the sea again, crowd so massive He hopped in a boat, sat down, whole squad on shore.
He dropped bars in parables, teachin heavy.
“Listen up: a sower went out to plant.”
“As he tossed seed, some fell by the road, birds swooped, ate it.”
“Some fell on rocky ground, no depth, sprouted fast.”
“But sun scorched it, no root, it withered.”
“Some fell among thorns, thorns grew, choked it, no fruit.”
“Some fell on good soil, grew, multiplied—thirty, sixty, hundred fold.”
He said: “Who got ears, hear this.”
When He was alone, crew and twelve asked about parables.
He said: “Y’all get kingdom secrets, outsiders get parables only.”
“So they see but don’t perceive, hear but don’t get it, lest they turn and get forgiven.”
He said: “Don’t you get this parable? How will you get any?”
“Sower sows the Word.”
“Those by the road hear, Satan snatches Word quick.”
“Those on rocky ground hear, receive with hype,
but no root, when trouble or persecution hits, they dip.”
“Those among thorns hear,
but life’s worries, money chase, and desires choke Word, no fruit.”
“Those on good soil hear, receive, bear fruit—thirty, sixty, hundred fold.”
He said: “Lamp ain’t for hiding under basket or bed, it’s for stand.”
“Nothing hidden stays hidden, it’ll be revealed.”
“If you got ears, hear.”
He said: “Pay attention. With measure you use, it’ll be measured back, plus more.”
“Whoever has, more will be given. Whoever lacks, even what he has will be taken.”
He said: “Kingdom of God is like a man tossin seed on ground,
sleeps, wakes, seed grows, he don’t know how.”
“Earth produces by itself—first blade, then head, then full grain.”
“When grain’s ripe, he swings sickle, harvest time.”
He said: “Kingdom of God is like mustard seed,
smallest seed when sown,
but grows big, branches wide, birds chill in shade.”
With many parables He spoke Word as they could handle.
Without parable He didn’t speak, but privately explained to His crew.
Same day evening He said: “Let’s cross to the other side.”
They left crowd, took Him in boat, other boats with them.
Big storm hit, waves crashed into boat, filling it.
He was asleep on cushion, they woke Him: “Teacher, don’t You care we perish?”
He got up, rebuked wind, said to sea: “Peace, chill.” Wind stopped, calm hit.
He said: “Why y’all scared? No faith?”
They were shook, said: “Who is this? Even wind and sea obey Him.”
They crossed over, landed in the country of the Gadarenes.
Soon as He stepped out the boat, a man with unclean spirit ran up from the tombs.
Dude lived in tombs, no one could chain him, not even with iron.
He’d been chained often, but broke chains, smashed shackles—no one strong enough to tame him.
Night and day he was in tombs and mountains, screaming, cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus far off, he sprinted, bowed down.
He shouted loud: “What You want with me, Jesus Son of the Most High God? Don’t torment me!”
Jesus had said: “Come out of the man, unclean spirit.”
He asked: “What’s your name?” Spirit said: “Legion, we many.”
He begged not to be sent away out of the country.
Big herd of pigs chillin nearby on the mountain.
Spirits begged: “Send us into pigs, let us enter.”
Jesus gave permission, unclean spirits entered pigs, herd rushed down cliff into sea, drowned—about two thousand.
Herd keepers ran, told it in city and country, people came to see.
They saw the man who had legion, sitting, clothed, sane. They were shook.
Witnesses told how it happened to the possessed man and about the pigs.
Crowd begged Him to leave their region.
As He got in boat, the man who was freed begged to roll with Him.
Jesus said: “Nah, go home, tell your people what the Lord did for you, how He showed mercy.”
Dude went, spread in Decapolis what Jesus did, everyone marveled.
Jesus crossed back in boat, big crowd gathered, He was by sea.
One of synagogue rulers, Jairus, came, fell at His feet.
He begged: “My little daughter’s dying. Come lay hands so she may live.”
Jesus went with him, big crowd followed, pressed Him.
A woman with blood issue twelve years,
had suffered under many docs, spent all she had, no better, worse.
She heard of Jesus, came in crowd, touched His clothes.
She said: “If I touch His clothes, I’ll be healed.”
Instantly blood dried, she felt healed.
Jesus felt power leave, turned: “Who touched My clothes?”
Disciples said: “Crowd’s pressing You, and You ask who touched?”
He looked around to see who did it.
Woman, fearing, trembling, knowing what happened, came, fell before Him, told truth.
He said: “Daughter, your faith healed you. Go in peace, be whole.”
While He spoke, people came from ruler’s house: “Your daughter’s dead, don’t bother Teacher.”
Jesus heard, said: “Don’t fear, just believe.”
He let no one follow except Peter, James, and John.
He came to ruler’s house, saw commotion, people weeping loud.
He said: “Why y’all crying? Child not dead, just sleeping.”
They laughed Him off. He put them all out, took child’s parents and His crew, entered room.
He took child’s hand, said: “Talitha cumi” (Girl, I say to you, arise).
Instantly girl got up, walked—she was twelve. Crowd was shook.
He charged them strictly no one should know, told them to give her food.
He bounced from there, came to His hometown, His crew followed.
Sabbath hit, He taught in synagogue. People were shook: “Where He get this wisdom and power?”
“Isn’t this the carpenter, Mary’s son, bro of James, Joses, Judas, Simon? Sisters here too.” They got offended.
Jesus said: “Prophet gets no honor except in his own hood, fam, and house.”
He couldn’t do many mighty works there, except heal a few sick by laying hands.
He marveled at their unbelief, went around villages teaching.
He called the twelve, sent them two by two, gave them authority over unclean spirits.
He commanded: “Take nothing for journey except staff—no bag, no bread, no money.”
“Wear sandals, don’t pack extra drip.”
“Wherever you enter a house, stay till you bounce from that place.”
“If they don’t vibe with you, shake dust off your feet as testimony.”
They went out, preached repentance.
Cast demons, anointed sick with oil, healed them.
King Herod heard, Jesus’ name viral. Some said: “John the Baptist risen, that’s why power works.”
Others: “He’s Elijah.” Others: “He’s a prophet.”
Herod said: “It’s John, whom I beheaded, risen.”
For Herod had arrested John cuz of Herodias, his bro Philip’s wife, whom he married.
John said: “It’s not lawful you have her.”
Herodias held grudge, wanted him dead, but couldn’t.
Herod feared John, knowing he was righteous and holy, kept him safe. He listened, was perplexed, yet enjoyed hearing him.
On Herod’s birthday, he threw a feast for nobles, captains, Galilee big shots.
Herodias’ daughter came, danced, pleased Herod and guests. King said: “Ask whatever, I’ll give.”
He swore: “Whatever you ask, up to half my kingdom.”
She went to her mom: “What should I ask?” Mom said: “Head of John the Baptist.”
She rushed to king: “I want John’s head on a platter now.”
King was sad, but cuz of oaths and guests, he didn’t refuse.
He sent executioner, commanded John’s head. He beheaded him in prison.
Brought head on platter, gave to girl, she gave to her mom.
John’s disciples heard, came, took his body, laid it in tomb.
Apostles gathered to Jesus, told Him all they did and taught.
He said: “Come rest in a desert place.” Crowd was heavy, no leisure even to eat.
They went by boat to desert place privately.
Crowd saw, recognized, ran on foot from cities, arrived before them.
Jesus saw big crowd, had compassion, they were like sheep without shepherd. He taught them much.
Day was far spent, disciples said: “This is desert, time’s late.”
“Send them away to villages to buy food.”
He said: “You give them food.” They said: “Should we buy two hundred pennyworth of bread?”
He said: “How many loaves? Go see.” They said: “Five, and two fish.”
He commanded them to sit in groups on green grass.
They sat in ranks, by hundreds and fifties.
He took five loaves and two fish, looked to heaven, blessed, broke, gave to disciples to set before them.
They all ate, were filled.
They took up twelve baskets full of leftovers.
Those who ate were about five thousand men.
Straightway He made disciples get in boat, go to Bethsaida, while He sent crowd away.
He sent them off, went to mountain to pray.
Evening came, boat was in middle of sea, He alone on land.
He saw them straining at rowing, wind against them. About fourth watch He came walking on sea, would’ve passed by.
They saw Him walking, thought it was a ghost, cried out.
They all saw, were shook. He said: “Chill, it’s Me, don’t fear.”
He went into boat, wind stopped. They were amazed beyond measure.
They hadn’t understood about loaves, hearts hardened.
They crossed, came to land of Gennesaret, anchored.
When they came out, people recognized Him.
They ran through region, carried sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.
Wherever He entered villages, cities, country, they laid sick in streets, begged to touch His garment edge. Whoever touched was healed.
Pharisees and some scribes from Jerusalem pulled up to Him.
They saw His crew eat bread with unwashed hands—straight up broke tradition.
Pharisees and all Jews don’t eat unless they wash hands, holding elders’ tradition.
When they come from market, they don’t eat unless they wash. They hold many wash rituals—cups, pots, brass vessels, tables.
Pharisees and scribes asked: “Why Your crew eat bread with unwashed hands, not walking by elders’ tradition?”
He said: “Isaiah called it—hypocrites. This people honor Me with lips, but heart far away.
They worship vain, teaching human rules as doctrine.
Y’all ditch God’s command, hold human tradition—washings, rituals.”
He said: “Full send reject God’s command to keep your tradition.
Moses said: Honor father and mother. Whoever curses them dies.
But y’all say: If a man says to father or mother, ‘It’s Corban’ (gift to God),
then he’s free from helping parents.
You cancel God’s Word with tradition. And many such things you do.”
He called crowd, said: “Listen, understand.
Nothing outside entering a man defiles him; what comes out defiles.”
If anyone got ears, hear.
When He entered house from crowd, disciples asked about parable.
He said: “Y’all still don’t get it? Whatever enters from outside can’t defile,
cuz it doesn’t enter heart but belly, goes out to sewer.” He declared all foods clean.
He said: “What comes out of man defiles.
From inside, heart, come evil thoughts: adulteries, fornications, murders,
thefts, coveting, wickedness, deceit, lust, envy, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
All these evil come from inside, defile man.”
He rose, went to Tyre and Sidon region, entered house, wanted no one to know, but couldn’t hide.
A woman whose daughter had unclean spirit heard, came, fell at His feet.
Woman was Greek, Syrophoenician by nation. She begged Him to cast demon out of daughter.
Jesus said: “Let children eat first. It’s not right to take kids’ bread, throw to dogs.”
She said: “Yes Lord, but dogs under table eat crumbs.”
He said: “For this word, go, demon gone from daughter.”
She went home, found child lying on bed, demon gone.
He left Tyre, went through Sidon to Sea of Galilee, into Decapolis.
They brought Him a deaf man with speech issue, begged Him to lay hand.
He took him aside, put fingers in ears, spit, touched tongue.
Looked to heaven, sighed, said: “Ephphatha” (be opened).
Instantly ears opened, tongue loosed, he spoke plain.
He charged them not to tell, but the more He charged, the more they spread.
They were beyond amazed: “He does all things well—makes deaf hear, mute speak.”
In those days, big crowd gathered, no food.
Jesus said to His crew: “I’m feelin for this crowd, they been with Me three days, no food.”
“If I send them home hungry, they’ll faint on the way, some came far.”
Disciples said: “How can anyone feed these here in desert with bread?”
He asked: “How many loaves?” They said: “Seven.”
He told crowd to sit, took seven loaves, gave thanks, broke, gave to disciples to serve.
They had a few small fish, He blessed, told them to serve too.
They ate, were filled, leftovers seven baskets.
About four thousand ate, He sent them away.
Straightway He got in boat with disciples, came to Dalmanutha.
Pharisees came, argued, asked for sign from heaven to test Him.
He sighed deep: “Why this generation seek sign? No sign given.”
He left, got in boat, crossed over.
Crew forgot bread, only one loaf in boat.
He warned: “Watch out for leaven of Pharisees and Herod.”
They reasoned: “It’s cuz we got no bread.”
Jesus knew, said: “Why reason no bread? Don’t you see, understand? Hearts hardened?
Eyes but don’t see, ears but don’t hear? Don’t remember?
When I broke five loaves for five thousand, how many baskets leftover?” They said: “Twelve.”
“And seven loaves for four thousand, how many baskets leftover?” They said: “Seven.”
He said: “How you still don’t get it?”
He came to Bethsaida, they brought blind man, begged Him to touch.
He took blind man by hand, led him out, spit on eyes, laid hands, asked: “See anything?”
He looked: “I see men like trees walking.”
Jesus laid hands again, eyes cleared, saw everything sharp.
He sent him home: “Don’t go into town.”
Jesus and His crew went to villages of Caesarea Philippi. On way He asked: “Who do people say I am?”
They said: “John Baptist, others Elijah, others one of prophets.”
He asked: “But who do you say I am?” Peter said: “You the Christ.”
He charged them not to tell anyone.
He began to teach: “Son of Man must suffer, be rejected by elders, chief priests, scribes, be killed, after three days rise.”
He spoke openly. Peter took Him aside, rebuked Him.
He turned, looked at disciples, rebuked Peter: “Get behind Me, Satan. You not mindful of God’s things, but man’s.”
He called crowd with disciples: “If anyone wants to follow, deny self, take up cross, follow Me.
Whoever wants to save life will lose it, whoever loses life for Me and gospel will save it.
What’s it profit to gain world, lose soul?
What can man give in exchange for soul?
Whoever’s ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous, sinful generation, Son of Man will be ashamed when He comes in glory of Father with angels.”
He said: “Truth drop—some here won’t taste death till they see kingdom of God come with power.”
Six days later He took Peter, James, John up a high mountain, alone. He got transfigured—glow mode.
His clothes went ultra white, no bleach on earth could flex that.
Elijah and Moses pulled up, chatting with Him.
Peter said: “Master, it’s lit we’re here. Let’s build three tents—one for You, one for Moses, one for Elijah.”
He said that cuz he was shook, didn’t know what to say.
Cloud covered, voice came: “This is My beloved Son, listen to Him.”
Suddenly they looked, saw no one but Jesus.
As they came down, He charged them not to tell anyone till Son of Man rose from dead.
They kept it, questioned what “rise from dead” meant.
They asked: “Why scribes say Elijah must come first?”
He said: “Elijah comes first, restores all. But Son of Man must suffer, be rejected.”
“Elijah already came, they did what they wanted, just as written.”
When they came to disciples, big crowd around, scribes arguing.
Crowd saw Him, amazed, ran to greet.
He asked: “What y’all arguing?”
One said: “Master, I brought my son with dumb spirit.
Wherever it grabs him, he foams, grinds teeth, stiffens. I asked disciples, they couldn’t cast it out.”
He said: “O faithless generation, how long I gotta be with y’all? Bring him.”
They brought him, spirit saw Jesus, convulsed, he fell, foamed.
Jesus asked father: “How long has this been?” He said: “Since childhood.
Often casts him into fire, water to destroy. If You can, help us.”
Jesus said: “If you can believe, all things possible.”
Father cried: “I believe, help my unbelief.”
Jesus saw crowd running, rebuked spirit: “Dumb and deaf spirit, I command, come out, don’t enter again.”
Spirit screamed, convulsed, came out. Boy looked dead, many said: “He’s gone.”
Jesus took his hand, lifted him, he arose.
Disciples asked privately: “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”
He said: “This kind only comes out by prayer.”
They left, passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know.
He taught: “Son of Man delivered, killed, after three days rise.”
They didn’t understand, feared to ask.
He came to Capernaum. In house He asked: “What were y’all disputing?”
They kept quiet, cuz on way they argued who’s greatest.
He sat, called twelve: “If anyone wants to be first, be last, servant of all.”
He took a child, set him in middle, hugged him.
He said: “Whoever receives one child in My name receives Me, and Him who sent Me.”
John said: “Master, we saw someone casting demons in Your name, he doesn’t follow us, we stopped him.”
Jesus said: “Don’t stop him. No one who does mighty work in My name can soon speak evil of Me.
Whoever’s not against us is for us.
Whoever gives you a cup of water cuz you belong to Christ won’t lose reward.”
“Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe to stumble, better for him to have millstone tied, thrown in sea.”
“If your hand makes you stumble, cut it off. Better enter life maimed than go to hell fire with two hands.
Where worm doesn’t die, fire not quenched.”
“If your foot makes you stumble, cut it off. Better enter life lame than be cast into hell with two feet.
Where worm doesn’t die, fire not quenched.”
“If your eye makes you stumble, pluck it out. Better enter kingdom with one eye than be cast into hell with two.
Where worm doesn’t die, fire not quenched.”
“Everyone will be salted with fire.”
“Salt is good, but if salt loses vibe, how restore? Have salt in yourselves, be at peace with each other.”
He left, came to Judea and beyond Jordan. Crowd pulled up again, He taught them as usual.
Pharisees asked: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” testing Him.
He said: “What did Moses command?”
They said: “Moses allowed writing divorce paper, sending her away.”
Jesus said: “He wrote that cuz of your hard vibes.
But from the start God made them male and female.
For this cause man leaves father and mother, joins wife.
Two become one flesh. No longer two, but one.
What God joined, don’t let man split.”
In house disciples asked again.
He said: “Whoever divorces wife, marries another, commits adultery.
If woman divorces husband, marries another, she commits adultery.”
They brought children to Him, disciples tried to block.
Jesus saw, was displeased: “Let kids come, don’t stop them. Kingdom of God belongs to such.”
“Whoever doesn’t receive kingdom like child won’t enter.”
He hugged kids, blessed them.
As He went out, a man ran, kneeled: “Good Master, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said: “Why call Me good? None good but God.”
“You know commandments: don’t kill, don’t commit adultery, don’t steal, don’t lie, don’t defraud, honor father and mother.”
He said: “Master, I kept all since youth.”
Jesus looked, loved him, said: “One thing missing: sell what you got, give to poor, treasure in heaven, then follow Me.”
He was sad, went away grieved, had great wealth.
Jesus looked around: “How hard for rich to enter kingdom.”
Disciples were shocked. Jesus said: “Children, how hard to enter kingdom.
Easier for camel to go through needle’s eye than rich to enter kingdom.”
They were astonished: “Who then can be saved?”
Jesus said: “With men impossible, but not with God. With God all possible.”
Peter said: “We left all, followed You.”
Jesus said: “Truly, whoever left house, bros, sisters, parents, children, lands for Me and gospel,
will receive hundredfold now—houses, family, lands, with persecutions—and eternal life later.
But many first will be last, last first.”
They were on way to Jerusalem, Jesus went ahead. Disciples were amazed, others afraid. He took twelve, told them what would happen.
“Son of Man delivered to chief priests, scribes, condemned to death, delivered to Gentiles.
They’ll mock, scourge, spit, kill Him. After three days He’ll rise.”
James and John came: “Master, we want You to do whatever we ask.”
He said: “What you want?”
They said: “Grant us to sit, one on Your right, one on Your left, in glory.”
Jesus said: “You don’t know what you ask. Can you drink My cup, be baptized with My baptism?”
They said: “We can.” Jesus said: “You will drink, be baptized.
But seats at right and left not Mine to give, prepared for others.”
Ten heard, got mad at James and John.
Jesus called them: “You know rulers of Gentiles lord it over them.
But not so among you. Whoever wants to be great must be servant.
Whoever wants to be chief must be slave of all.
Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, give His life ransom for many.”
They came to Jericho. As He left with disciples and crowd, blind Bartimaeus sat begging.
He heard Jesus of Nazareth, cried: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.”
Many told him to chill, but he cried louder: “Son of David, have mercy.”
Jesus stopped, said: “Call him.” They called: “Cheer up, rise, He calls you.”
He threw off cloak, rose, came to Jesus.
Jesus asked: “What you want Me to do?” He said: “Lord, that I may see.”
Jesus said: “Go, your faith healed you.” Instantly he saw, followed Jesus on the way.
When they came near Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany at Mount of Olives, He sent two disciples.
He said: “Go to village ahead, you’ll find a colt tied, never ridden. Untie, bring it.
If anyone asks, say: ‘The Lord needs it, will send it back.’”
They went, found colt tied by door outside, untied it.
People standing said: “Why you untying colt?”
They said what Jesus commanded, people let them go.
They brought colt to Jesus, threw clothes on it, He sat.
Many spread clothes on road, others cut branches, laid them.
Crowd ahead and behind shouted: “Hosanna! Blessed is He that comes in name of Lord.
Blessed is kingdom of David our father that comes. Hosanna in highest.”
Jesus entered Jerusalem, into temple, looked around. Evening came, He went to Bethany with twelve.
Next day, leaving Bethany, He was hungry.
He saw fig tree afar with leaves, came to see fruit, found none, only leaves—it wasn’t season.
Jesus said: “No one eat fruit from you forever.” Disciples heard.
They came to Jerusalem. He entered temple, began to cast out sellers and buyers, overturned tables of money changers and seats of dove sellers.
He didn’t allow anyone to carry stuff through temple.
He taught: “Isn’t it written, My house shall be called house of prayer for all nations? But you made it den of thieves.”
Scribes and chief priests heard, sought to destroy Him, feared Him cuz crowd was astonished at His teaching.
When evening came, He went out of city.
Morning, they passed fig tree, saw it dried from roots.
Peter remembered, said: “Master, look, fig tree You cursed is withered.”
Jesus said: “Have faith in God.
Truly, whoever says to mountain, ‘Be removed, cast into sea,’ and doesn’t doubt but believes, it’ll happen.
Whatever you ask in prayer, believe you receive, and you’ll have it.
When you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so Father may forgive you.
But if you don’t forgive, Father won’t forgive your trespasses.”
They came again to Jerusalem. As He walked in temple, chief priests, scribes, elders came.
They said: “By what authority do You do these things? Who gave You authority?”
Jesus said: “I’ll ask one thing, answer Me, then I’ll tell you by what authority.
Was John’s baptism from heaven or men? Answer.”
They reasoned: “If we say heaven, He’ll say, why didn’t you believe?
If we say men, they feared people, cuz all counted John as prophet.”
They answered: “We don’t know.” Jesus said: “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He started droppin parables: “A man planted vineyard, set hedge, dug winepress, built tower, rented it to farmers, bounced.”
“Season came, he sent servant to farmers to get fruit.”
“They grabbed him, beat him, sent him away empty.”
“He sent another, they threw stones, wounded head, sent him shamefully.”
“He sent more, some they killed, some beat.”
“Still one left, his beloved son. He sent him, saying: They’ll respect my son.”
“Farmers said: This is heir, let’s kill him, grab inheritance.”
“They killed him, threw him out of vineyard.”
“What will owner do? He’ll come, destroy farmers, give vineyard to others.”
“Didn’t you read: Stone builders rejected became head cornerstone.
Lord did this, it’s marvelous.”
They sought to arrest Him, feared crowd, knew He spoke parable against them, left.
They sent Pharisees and Herodians to trap Him in words.
They said: “Master, we know You true, don’t care for man’s face, teach God’s way. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar?”
“Should we give or not?” He knew their hypocrisy: “Why tempt Me? Bring coin.”
They brought. He said: “Whose image, superscription?” They said: “Caesar’s.”
Jesus said: “Render to Caesar what’s Caesar’s, to God what’s God’s.” They marveled.
Sadducees came, who say no resurrection. They asked:
“Moses wrote: If brother dies, leaves wife, no child, his brother takes her, raises seed.
Seven bros, first took wife, died, no seed.
Second took her, died, no seed.
Third likewise, all seven, no seed. Last of all woman died.
In resurrection, whose wife?”
Jesus said: “Aren’t you wrong, not knowing scriptures or God’s power?
When they rise, they neither marry nor are given, but are like angels.”
“About dead rising, haven’t you read in Moses’ book, bush passage, how God said: I am God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob?
He’s not God of dead, but of living. You’re way off.”
One scribe asked: “Which commandment is first?”
Jesus said: “First: Hear O Israel, Lord our God is one Lord.
Love Lord your God with all heart, soul, mind, strength.
Second: Love neighbor as yourself. No command greater.”
Scribe said: “Well said, Master. God is one, no other.
To love Him with all heart, understanding, strength, and neighbor as self is more than all burnt offerings.”
Jesus saw he answered wisely: “You’re not far from kingdom.” No one dared ask more.
Jesus taught in temple: “How say scribes Christ is son of David?
David himself said by Spirit: Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand till I make enemies footstool.
David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?” Crowd heard gladly.
He said: “Beware scribes, who love long robes, greetings in markets,
chief seats in synagogues, chief rooms at feasts.
They devour widows’ houses, for show make long prayers. They’ll receive greater damnation.”
Jesus sat opposite treasury, watched people cast money. Many rich cast much.
Poor widow came, threw two mites.
He called disciples: “Truly, this poor widow gave more than all.
They gave out of abundance, she gave all she had, her whole living.”
As He left temple, one disciple said: “Master, peep these stones, these buildings.”
Jesus said: “You see these? Not one stone left on another, all thrown down.”
He sat on Mount of Olives opposite temple. Peter, James, John, Andrew asked privately,
“Tell us, when will these things be? What’s the sign when all fulfilled?”
Jesus said: “Take heed no one deceives you.
Many will come in My name, saying, I am Christ, and deceive many.
When you hear wars, rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. These must happen, but end not yet.
Nation will rise against nation, kingdom against kingdom. Earthquakes, famines in places—these are beginnings of sorrows.”
“Watch yourselves. They’ll deliver you to councils, beat you in synagogues, brought before rulers and kings for My sake, testimony to them.
Gospel must first be preached to all nations.
When they arrest you, don’t premeditate what to speak. Whatever given in that hour, speak. It’s not you speaking, but Holy Spirit.
Brother will betray brother to death, father child, children rise against parents, cause them to be put to death.
You’ll be hated by all for My name’s sake. But whoever endures to end will be saved.”
“When you see abomination of desolation standing where it shouldn’t (reader understand), then those in Judea flee to mountains.
Whoever on housetop don’t go down, don’t enter house to take anything.
Whoever in field don’t turn back to take clothes.
Woe to pregnant and nursing in those days.
Pray your flight not in winter.
For in those days tribulation such as never before since creation, nor ever shall be.
Unless Lord shortened days, no flesh saved. But for elect’s sake He shortened days.
If anyone says: Look, here’s Christ, or there, don’t believe.
False Christs, false prophets will rise, show signs, wonders, to deceive, if possible, even elect.
But take heed, I told you all beforehand.”
“In those days, after tribulation, sun darkened, moon won’t give light,
stars fall, powers of heaven shaken.
Then they’ll see Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
He’ll send angels, gather His elect from four winds, from earth’s end to heaven’s end.”
“Learn parable of fig tree: When branch tender, leaves sprout, you know summer near.
So when you see these things, know it’s near, even at doors.
Truly, this generation won’t pass till all fulfilled.
Heaven and earth pass away, but My words won’t.”
“But of that day and hour no one knows, not angels, not Son, only Father.
Take heed, watch, pray, for you don’t know when time is.
It’s like man going far country, left house, gave authority to servants, to each his work, commanded porter to watch.
Watch therefore, for you don’t know when master of house comes—at evening, midnight, cockcrow, or morning.
Lest coming suddenly he finds you sleeping.
What I say to you, I say to all: Watch.”
Two days till Passover and Feast of Unleavened Bread. Chief priests and scribes plotted to grab Him by stealth, kill Him.
They said: “Not on feast day, lest crowd riot.”
He was in Bethany at Simon the leper’s house. A woman came with alabaster box of costly ointment, broke it, poured on His head.
Some were mad: “Why waste this ointment?
It could’ve been sold for much, given to poor.” They scolded her.
Jesus said: “Leave her alone. She did good work for Me.
Poor you’ll always have, Me not always.
She did what she could, anointed My body for burial.
Wherever gospel preached, her act will be told.”
Judas Iscariot, one of twelve, went to chief priests to betray Him.
They were glad, promised money. He sought chance to betray Him.
First day of Unleavened Bread, when they killed Passover lamb, disciples asked: “Where should we prep Passover?”
He sent two: “Go into city, meet man carrying water. Follow him.
Say to house master: The Master says, Where’s guest room to eat Passover with disciples?
He’ll show large upper room furnished, ready. Prep there.”
Disciples went, found as He said, prepped Passover.
Evening came, He sat with twelve.
As they ate, Jesus said: “Truly, one of you eating with Me will betray Me.”
They were sad, said one by one: “Is it I?”
He said: “It’s one of twelve, who dips with Me in dish.
Son of Man goes as written, but woe to betrayer—it’d be better he wasn’t born.”
As they ate, Jesus took bread, blessed, broke, gave: “Take, eat, this is My body.”
He took cup, gave thanks, gave: they all drank.
He said: “This is My blood of new covenant, shed for many.
I won’t drink fruit of vine till I drink it new in kingdom of God.”
They sang hymn, went to Mount of Olives.
Jesus said: “All of you will stumble tonight. It’s written: I’ll smite shepherd, sheep scattered.
But after I rise, I’ll go before you to Galilee.”
Peter said: “Though all stumble, not me.”
Jesus said: “Truly, before cock crows twice, you’ll deny Me thrice.”
He said more: “If I die with You, I won’t deny.” They all said same.
They came to Gethsemane. He said: “Sit here while I pray.”
He took Peter, James, John, began to be sore amazed, heavy.
He said: “My soul sorrowful to death. Stay here, watch.”
He went forward, fell, prayed if possible hour pass.
He said: “Abba, Father, all things possible. Take cup away. Yet not My will, but Yours.”
He came, found them sleeping: “Simon, you sleep? Couldn’t watch one hour?
Watch, pray, lest you enter temptation. Spirit ready, flesh weak.”
He went again, prayed same words.
He returned, found them asleep again, eyes heavy, didn’t know what to answer.
He came third time: “Sleep on now, take rest. Enough, hour come. Son of Man betrayed into sinners’ hands.
Rise, let’s go. Betrayer near.”
Immediately Judas came, one of twelve, with crowd armed with swords, staves, from chief priests, scribes, elders.
Betrayer gave sign: “Whom I kiss, He’s the one. Grab Him, lead away safely.”
He came, kissed Him: “Master, Master.”
They laid hands, grabbed Him.
One standing drew sword, struck servant of high priest, cut off ear.
Jesus said: “Are you come out with swords, staves to take Me like thief?
Daily I was with you in temple teaching, you didn’t grab Me. But scriptures must be fulfilled.”
All His crew fled.
A young man followed, clothed with linen cloth, crowd grabbed him.
He left cloth, fled naked.
They led Jesus to high priest. All chief priests, elders, scribes gathered.
Peter followed afar, into palace, sat with servants, warmed himself.
Chief priests sought witness against Jesus to kill Him, found none.
Many bore false witness, but testimonies didn’t agree.
Some stood, false witness:
“We heard Him say, I’ll destroy temple made with hands, build another without hands in three days.”
Their witness didn’t agree.
High priest stood: “Answer nothing? What do these witness against You?”
He held His peace, answered nothing. High priest asked: “Are You Christ, Son of Blessed?”
Jesus said: “I am. You’ll see Son of Man sitting at right hand of power, coming in clouds.”
High priest tore clothes: “What need we witnesses?
You heard blasphemy. What think?” They all condemned Him guilty of death.
Some began to spit, cover His face, buffet Him, say: “Prophesy.” Servants struck Him.
Peter was below in palace, one maid of high priest came.
She saw Peter warming, looked: “You were with Jesus of Nazareth.”
He denied: “I don’t know, don’t understand.” He went out to porch, cock crowed.
Maid saw him again, said to bystanders: “This is one of them.”
He denied again. Later bystanders said: “Surely you’re one of them, you’re Galilean.”
He cursed, swore: “I don’t know this man you speak of.”
Cock crowed second time. Peter remembered Jesus’ word: “Before cock crow twice, you’ll deny Me thrice.” He broke down, wept.
Straightway in morning, chief priests with elders, scribes, whole council held meeting, bound Jesus, carried Him to Pilate.
Pilate asked: “Are You King of Jews?” He answered: “You said it.”
Chief priests accused Him of many things.
Pilate asked again: “Don’t You answer? See how many things they witness against You.”
But Jesus still answered nothing, Pilate marveled.
At feast he released one prisoner, whoever crowd asked.
There was Barabbas, chained with rebels, who committed murder in uprising.
Crowd shouted, asked Pilate to do as he always did.
Pilate answered: “Do you want me to release King of Jews?”
He knew chief priests delivered Him out of envy.
But priests stirred crowd to ask for Barabbas instead.
Pilate said: “What then should I do with Him you call King of Jews?”
They shouted: “Crucify Him.”
Pilate said: “Why, what evil has He done?” They shouted louder: “Crucify Him.”
Pilate, willing to satisfy crowd, released Barabbas, delivered Jesus after scourging to be crucified.
Soldiers led Him into hall called Praetorium, called whole band.
They clothed Him with purple, plaited crown of thorns, put it on Him.
They mocked: “Hail, King of Jews.”
They struck His head with reed, spit on Him, bowed knees in fake worship.
After mocking, they stripped purple, put His own clothes, led Him out to crucify.
They compelled Simon of Cyrene, father of Alexander and Rufus, coming from country, to bear His cross.
They brought Him to Golgotha, meaning Place of a Skull.
They gave Him wine mixed with myrrh, He didn’t take.
They crucified Him, parted His garments, casting lots what each should take.
It was third hour, they crucified Him.
Superscription of His accusation written: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
With Him they crucified two thieves, one on right, one on left.
Scripture fulfilled: He was numbered with transgressors.
Passersby railed, wagged heads: “You that destroy temple, build in three days,
save Yourself, come down from cross.”
Likewise chief priests mocking among scribes said: “He saved others, Himself He can’t save.
Let Christ King of Israel descend now from cross, that we may see, believe.” Those crucified with Him reviled Him.
When sixth hour came, darkness over whole land till ninth hour.
At ninth hour Jesus cried loud: “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” meaning, “My God, My God, why You forsake Me?”
Some standing said: “He calls Elijah.”
One ran, filled sponge with vinegar, put on reed, gave Him to drink: “Let’s see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
Jesus cried loud, gave up the ghost.
Veil of temple torn in two from top to bottom.
Centurion standing opposite saw He cried out, gave up ghost, said: “Truly this man was Son of God.”
Women looked afar: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James the less and Joses, and Salome.
They followed Him, ministered, and many other women came up with Him to Jerusalem.
When evening came, cuz it was Preparation, day before Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathaea, honorable counselor, who waited for kingdom of God, came boldly to Pilate, asked for Jesus’ body.
Pilate marveled He was already dead, called centurion, asked if long dead.
When he knew from centurion, he gave body to Joseph.
Joseph bought linen, took Him down, wrapped, laid Him in tomb hewn out of rock, rolled stone to door.
Mary Magdalene and Mary of Joses saw where He was laid.
When Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome bought spices to anoint Him.
Early morning, first day of week, they came to tomb at sunrise.
They said: “Who gonna roll away stone from tomb door?”
They looked, saw stone rolled away—it was massive.
Entering tomb, they saw young man in white robe sitting on right side, they were shook.
He said: “Don’t be scared. You seek Jesus of Nazareth, crucified. He’s risen, not here. Look at place they laid Him.
Go tell His disciples and Peter He goes before you into Galilee. You’ll see Him there, as He said.”
They fled from tomb, trembling, amazed. They said nothing to anyone, they were scared.
Now when Jesus rose early first day of week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom He cast seven demons.
She went, told those who had been with Him, mourning, weeping.
They heard He was alive, seen by her, didn’t believe.
After that He appeared in another form to two walking into country.
They went, told rest, they didn’t believe them either.
Later He appeared to eleven as they sat eating, rebuked unbelief and hardness of heart cuz they didn’t believe those who saw Him risen.
He said: “Go into all world, preach gospel to every creature.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved. Whoever doesn’t believe will be condemned.
These signs follow believers: In My name they cast demons, speak new tongues,
take up serpents, if they drink deadly thing it won’t hurt, lay hands on sick, they recover.”
After Lord spoke, He was received into heaven, sat at right hand of God.
They went out, preached everywhere, Lord working with them, confirming Word with signs following.
